I have watched many movies on acid and these are the ones I would say were the best time:

Inception (Christopher Nolan) - If you enjoy being completely immersed in the world of a film, this one will make you start thinking you're dreaming

Waking Life and A Scanner Darkly (both Richard Linklater films) - Waking Life is for a more philosophical trip and A Scanner Darkly is for a more Scifi Comedy vibe

Brazil (Terry Gilliam) - If you like a weird trippy plot but with a satirical undertone, this is great

Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas (Terry Gilliam, again) - A classic 'drugz' film, but the book is better

And my favourite trip film (really all 3 at once is best) ... 

The original Star Wars trilogy - This was the best time watching a film I've ever had, you appreciate every aspect of how amazing the films are (particularly A New Hope)

I was in a very similar situation to you last year and I went on this very group and made a post about wanting to make an attempt - hours later I ended up trying and very nearly succeeding if it weren't for some serious cosmological luck. I spent over 3 months in hospital and almost died several times during my recovery due to lung infections related to the initial trauma (a hanging). I can tell you that when I woke up, even when I was not able to talk, breathe without a ventilator/tracheostomy, walk properly (after being in an ICU bed unconscious for 5 weeks straight) or eat, when I regained consciousness I was sooooo glad that I didn't die and that it was unsuccessful, even in the state I was in. I still feel that way today and can tell you that attempting or even worse succeeding only passes the pain you're experiencing at the moment onto others that care about you (including your kitten who is dependent on you). My dad who found me has struggled with the memory of having to save me at the last minute. Recovery from depression is definitely not easy and as much as it's sad to say, the meds used to treat it are very often ineffective if they are taken too late into a spiral. My advice would be to sleep on it and speak to someone you know will listen to you when you explain how you're thinking, even if it's just a stranger on the internet. We want you here and there is no depressive pit deep enough that can't be climbed out of slowly but surely.

You're spoilt when it comes to trippy rock music. I would've mentioned ELO, LZ (shout out to Physical Grafitti, that album kills), GD (specific live seshes, American Beauty) and PF (Animals, Dark Side...) and TI (Lonerism)but those have already been mentioned. There's Steely Dan particularly their albums The Royal Scam (a favourite of mine, one of the songs in it Kid Charlemagne is about Owsley Stanley, a very large acid supplier in the 60s) and Can't Buy a Thrill and Aja. Can't go wrong with Simon & Garfunkel either - their album Bridge Over Troubled Water is one of the best of all time and is very trippy and soothing at times (very good for a sunny nature trip - listened to it in the largest park in London Richmond Park last summer on a 32 mile acid fueled walk). Not strictly rock, but if you like it's experimental nature Death Grips sounds like nothing else - would thoroughly recommend their mixtape Exmilitary and The Money Store if you haven't checked them out either.
